_comment: The maintainer's M4 Mac mini with 1b-class models, W3 of docs/FIVE_DAY_PLAN.md,
2026-11-28. Every size and context below was read off `ollama ps` / `/api/ps` on
a private runtime (127.0.0.1:11999, Ollama 0.40.16) on this machine.
Sizes are the resident footprint in GB at `fits` (8192), measured one model at
gemma3:1b 957,916,118. All three were resident together at 8192.

host.label: M4 Mac mini, 16 GB unified, 1b-class models
host.notes: Budget is what the agent reports: headroom.free_bytes 12884901888 (apple_wired_limit; iogpu.wired_limit_mb reads 0, so 75% of 16 GiB). scenarios.m4.json and the runbook say 11.6; the agent says 12.9. eviction_context measured for llama3.2:1b + qwen2.5:1.5b loaded together, both orders: both resident at 65536 (reproduced twice each order), evicted at 69632, 73728, 81920, 98304 and 131072. Combined footprint at the boundary does not bracket cleanly: 6.12 GB coexisted at 65536 while 5.95 GB evicted at 69632. qwen2.5:1.5b and gemma3:1b cap at 32768: the runtime clamps any larger num_ctx to 32768 (gemma3:1b 1.01 GB, qwen2.5:1.5b 2.12 GB there). So too_large_for_accelerator does NOT exceed the budget for gemma3:1b: 131072 is clamped to 32768 at 1.01 GB. No context makes the small model exceed the budget on this host; cpu_split is not inducible here on that ground as well as unified memory. Conditions during the run: the default Ollama app (:11434, not touched) had a llama3.1:8b llama-server runner alive (-c 4096, RSS 9 MB), swap 7.49 GB used of 8 GB at the start. The private agent was started with WICKLEE_LLAMACPP_PORT=11998 (nothing listening) because its llama.cpp process discovery otherwise attaches to Ollama's own llama-server runners, including the default runtime's.

_comment: resident_gb above is measured at `fits`. Measured on this host:
qwen2.5:1.5b 2.02-2.12 GB at 32768 (its maximum); gemma3:1b 1.01 GB at 32768
(its maximum). too_large_for_accelerator is clamped by the runtime and does
not exceed the budget for gemma3:1b; see host.notes.
For the reference controller. Workflow A holds `held` continuously.
Workflow B's step may run on any model in `acceptable`, in preference
order — the operator declares that, not Wicklee. `defer_allowed` lets
the wicklee policy wait rather than displace.
